title: Tensor adjunctions and preservation of limits from an exact pairing
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,\otimes,\mathbf1)$ be a monoidal category [def-sfb-monoidal-category]. Let $P,D\in\mathcal C$ have morphisms $e:D\otimes P\to\mathbf1$ and $c:\mathbf1\to P\otimes D$ satisfying $(1_P\otimes e)(c\otimes1_P)=1_P$ and $(e\otimes1_D)(1_D\otimes c)=1_D$, with associators and unitors understood. Such data are called an exact pairing. Put $T_A(B)=A\otimes B$ and $U_A(B)=B\otimes A$. Then there are adjunctions
$$T_D\dashv T_P,\qquad U_P\dashv U_D.$$
An adjunction $F\dashv G$ means a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(F(A),B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(A,G(B))$ natural in both variables. Each of the two right adjoints $T_P,U_D$ preserves every existing small limit, and each of the two left adjoints $T_D,U_P$ preserves every existing small colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Here a limit is an object with a compatible cone of maps to the diagram, universal among such cones; preservation means the image cone is again universal. In particular the right adjoints preserve products [def-weil-category-product]. Smallness is relative to [def-weil-size-convention].

The exact-pairing hypothesis is CategoryTheory.ExactPairing P D with coevaluation c and evaluation e. tensorLeftAdjunction P D (Basic.lean:459) gives T_D ⊣ T_P, and tensorRightAdjunction P D (Basic.lean:468) gives U_P ⊣ U_D. For either displayed adjunction adj, adj.leftAdjoint_preservesColimits (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Adjunction/Limits.lean:92) and adj.rightAdjoint_preservesLimits (same file:207) give its preservation clauses at any chosen small indexing universes; products are limits of discrete diagrams. No existence of a limit or colimit is asserted.
